newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Ciampi says no plan to delay EMU start.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ciampi says no plan to delay EMU start.

text.p: Italy's Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Thursday that there were no plans among European Union members to seek a delay in the planned 1999 start for economic and monetary union (EMU).

Ciampi spoke in an interview on TG3 Italian television news, which reported there was growing speculation an EU summit in Dublin on December 13 and 14 or EU finance ministers could discuss a possible delay in the schedule.
"None of these theories is on the table for the European Council, or for the finance ministers," Ciampi said.

The speculation appeared to have been driven by a cryptic comment on Wednesday night from Massimo D'Alema, whose Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) is the biggest in Italy's centre-left government coalition.
D'Alema had been quoted as speaking of a "development of major importance at a European level" on December 11 or 12.
Ciampi believed D'Alema was talking about "the importance of accelerating the process of political union" in the EU.
